architecture: LeNet-5 style CNN: conv5x5(1->6, pad 2) relu maxpool2, conv5x5(6->16) relu maxpool2, fc 400->120 relu, fc 120->84 relu, fc 84->10

input.layout: channel, row (top to bottom), column (left to right)
input.scaling: x = pixel / 255: 0.0 is the black background, 1.0 the brightest part of the article
input.dataset_facts: Fashion-MNIST (Xiao, Rasul and Vollgraf 2017, Zalando Research): front-view product photos of Zalando's catalogue converted to 28 x 28 greyscale. The conversion trimmed the edges close to the corner colour, resized the longest edge to 28 pixels, sharpened with a Gaussian operator (radius and standard deviation 1), extended the shorter edge to 28 with the article centred, negated the intensities (the article is bright on a black background) and converted to 8 bits. The held-out images are the dataset's official test set (10,000 images, 1,000 per class).

conv: cross-correlation as in PyTorch Conv2d: out[o, i, j] = bias[o] + sum_c sum_u sum_v weight[o, c, u, v] * in[c, i + u, j + v] (after zero padding)
flatten: the [16, 5, 5] map is flattened in (channel, row, column) order to 400 values
output: 10 logits, class k = the k-th entry of classes; the prediction is the argmax (logits within 1e-9 x max(1, |max logit|) of the maximum count as tied; ties go to the lowest index)
metric: accuracy on the 10,000 test images, 1,000 per class
